Closing evidence check: State what the contrasting example of ear training and transcription revealed that the first one did not. What ear training and transcription means here: Timbre is sound quality—the set of audible features that helps two sources or actions sound different even at a similar pitch and loudness. How the relationship changes the result: The material and action shape a sound’s beginning, continuation, and ending. A quick tap has a sharp attack and short decay; rubbed paper has a softer attack and continuing noise. Choice and tradeoff: A dense mix can feel full but mask individual layers. A sparse texture reveals timbre clearly but may reduce weight or momentum. Worked example: Tap a tabletop once, then rub one sheet of paper for the same count. Map each as ATTACK → SUSTAIN → DECAY and cite the moment that distinguishes them. A trusted adult may produce the two sounds if needed. Non-example: Calling one source “better” or naming an instrument family without citing an audible or supplied source feature is preference or recall, not listening evidence. 1. ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g9-arts-and-music-u02-l05

Lesson focus: ear training and transcription

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_MODEL

MODEL B — contrasting route for ear training and transcription. Reconnect: Timbre is sound quality—the set of audible features that helps two sources or actions sound different even at a similar pitch and loudness. Model A demonstrates: Tap a tabletop once, then rub one sheet of paper for the same count. Map each as ATTACK → SUSTAIN → DECAY and cite the moment that distinguishes them. A trusted adult may produce the two sounds if needed. Model B deliberately tests the opposite pressure described here: A dense mix can feel full but mask individual layers. A sparse texture reveals timbre clearly but may reduce weight or momentum. Compare the two by locating attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action; do not rank them by polish or resemblance. Mark which condition makes each route useful. Then make a third small case that borrows the relationship—not the model’s subject, sequence, wording, style, or interpretation. Use it to study ear training and transcription; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Model A recap and contrasting Model B as the two works for comparison; no earlier source file is required.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Tap, point through, gesture, or use the supplied notation or event map without recording. A written or notated response can show structure and reasoning; it does not claim hearing or performed control that was not actually demonstrated. No instrument, microphone, camera, or public performance is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres an aural element (ear training and transcription). Provide a fully equivalent non-aural route: notated, written, or graphic representation; visual or tactile pulse (a moving marker, a tapped or felt beat); and vibration or sight-reading in place of listening. Do not require the learner to hear a pitch, interval, or timbre to demonstrate understanding of it.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.fallback: Count, point through, tap, speak, gesture, or read the complete pulse and pitch map silently; no instrument, speaker, microphone, or recording is required.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce ear training and transcription to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one attack relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact attack evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply ear training and transcription under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on ear training and transcription rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
